## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷanāradajātaka* (Ja 477) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional introductory setting recorded in the text's blurb, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana to address the allurements of a coarse girl, opening with the verse line "No wood is chopt". The text is also cited in the post-canonical *Milindapañha* in the *Gharakapotaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.6.4).

In modern scholarship, the commentary to the *Cūḷanāradajātaka* has been examined for its socio-historical terminology, specifically regarding an occurrence of the term *Sākiya-bhikkhu* in an episode where a mother attempts to entrap a monk as a husband for her daughter [Williams, Critical Concepts].
